made.ark/fefc82879a35.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The device hums. Hammering, sawdust, and the biggest boat you have ever seen, sitting on dry land.
made.ark/8eab89d3cc3d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.
made.ark/69f96c9184f2.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
made.ark/67da24182ccc.m4a: bm_fable|0.9|0.88|Welcome. There is much to do before the animals come.
made.ark/95afffa1e3fc.m4a: bm_fable|0.9|0.88|Keep going. God told us to be ready.
made.ark/c2cc7f22c1cf.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Everyone is busy getting the ark ready.
made.ark/7e5469277c4b.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.
made.ark/f68593a9612c.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|An armful of grain. Carry it to the ark.
made.ark/8e349f25b2b2.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A basket of fruit. Carry it to the ark.
made.ark/c84d8c84faf4.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A jar of oil. Carry it to the ark.
made.ark/6c370b7d6eed.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The door of the ark stands open.
made.ark/c61571a78fd0.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The ramp up to the ark’s door.
made.ark/c7634ba9d474.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.
made.ark/0d03393697d5.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Long after, the book of Hebrews said:
made.ark/5a61b06cdefa.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|By faith Noah, when warned about things not yet seen, in godly fear built an ark to save his family.
made.ark/61f508418590.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Noah built for years with no rain in sight, because God had said so. Trusting God means doing what He says even before we see why.
made.ark/0512bb21ed9a.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.
made.ark/de0c6b59e4b3.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights
made.ark/d08c5575dc3a.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The two of them follow you.
made.ark/9c68894bb6e0.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Bring this pair to the ark first.
made.ark/deeb1eb1d17d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Bring the animals here, two by two.
made.ark/432f78484a02.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Up the ramp and into the ark they go.
made.ark/43a3a9a55448.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A dove watches from a branch.
made.ark/9af8762568d8.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
made.ark/666250a498ac.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And Noah and his wife, with his sons and their wives, entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.
made.ark/469d6972a4be.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And they entered, the male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the Lord shut him in.
made.ark/d7c7e2cea885.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|God Himself shut the door. Everyone inside was kept safe by Him.
made.ark/e39440e2e0e5.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
made.ark/83afa707c7b6.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
made.ark/f026277f178f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Your device buzzes hard. Time to go, right now!

made.ark/8112bad901a2.m4a: am_michael|1.0|1.0|The tar pit is up by the trees. Fill a jar for me.
made.ark/71faf47a548f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You fill a jar with pitch. Take it to Japheth.
made.ark/f8266dfc4637.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Japheth spreads the pitch along the hull.
made.ark/c909258469b0.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
made.ark/1af85afc2147.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
made.ark/eed9cf010176.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A cubit is about the length of a grown-up’s forearm. 300 cubits is about as long as one and a half football fields.

made.ark/259773d66b03.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Long after, the apostle Peter wrote that God:
made.ark/4309248900e5.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, among the eight;
made.ark/6d77eab6fccb.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Sheep and goats wait in the pen. There are more of these than two.
made.ark/fa5ac5fc67f6.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate; a pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate;
made.ark/402474e2d364.m4a: bm_daniel|1.0|1.0|I am Shem. My brothers are Ham and Japheth.
made.ark/3a6ba63c1db5.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
made.ark/97117fcc613e.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The glowing door nearby leads back to your time device.
made.ark/35449620d3a1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Your discoveries are saved. When you come back, the story picks up from this part.
made.ark/61bfad05a95f.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|God keeps His people safe. He asks us to trust Him and obey, even before we see why.
made.ark/de6d94a5c96f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Noah walked with God, in a world full of violence. (6:9-12)

made.ark/7576b7e8636d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The animals came two by two, and the Lord shut Noah in. (7:7-16)
made.ark/8092050394c2.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The rain fell for forty days and forty nights. (7:11-12)
made.ark/971c1989f48a.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You, and that you helped load the food, lead animals and carry pitch.
made.ark/f1b7f01d4d1c.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The neighbor, the wives’ looks, and what each of Noah’s family was doing.
made.ark/d881ac8ae9e0.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|How the ark looked. The Bible gives its size (6:15) but not its shape.
made.ark/ace899c2a9ba.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The Bible says everyone and everything outside the ark died in the flood (7:21-23). We did not show it. Read it together with a parent.
made.ark/b6dfa1200d9f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Twelve cards hide six pairs of animals. Turn two at a time and find every pair.
made.ark/cfaa7d9ded34.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Arrow keys and Space, or click a card. Find the pairs!
made.ark/38ab0f0ca742.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Every animal safe aboard, two by two.
made.babel/de892712fd67.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The device hums. A flat, dusty plain, smoke from a hundred kilns, and in the middle, a tower going up and up.
made.babel/c18967710e49.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.
made.babel/2e5b2f80c13b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
made.babel/ed0b8d5c357c.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|1.0|Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.
made.babel/078761d3294c.m4a: am_onyx|1.0|1.0|You there! Every hand helps. Dig clay, bake it, and stack the bricks on the tower.
made.babel/02da0b1e003d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A lump of wet clay. Bake it in the kiln.
made.babel/7fc216cf4dd0.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You set the clay in the kiln. It glows red...
made.babel/513cf8724a79.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A hard, baked brick! Take it to the tower.
made.babel/7c447c53f414.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|That brick is already baked. Take it to the tower.
made.babel/9fec4baf8cdd.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A stack of bricks, waiting to go up.
made.babel/e427258e4a32.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Up it goes onto the tower.
made.babel/da9a41c0843f.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|1.0|Come, let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.
made.babel/25a56e2dca80.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|They wanted to make a great name for themselves, instead of honoring God’s name.
made.babel/7f73c441b0ce.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then the Lord came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.
made.babel/fe35bf78eba2.m4a: af_heart|0.88|1.0|If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them. Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.
made.babel/7a9398e8fc1f.m4a: am_eric|1.0|0.95|From up there you will see the whole world.
made.babel/a150853c07ee.m4a: am_eric|1.0|0.95|Gorra fen tikka? Mo mo zandu! Plif?
made.babel/7e6ed49368eb.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|He points and waves his arms. You can’t understand a word.
made.babel/50befa2c62fa.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|She looks just as confused as you are.
made.babel/18932dc61de9.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Nobody can understand anybody. The builders put down their tools.
made.babel/deddb6e04a41.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So the Lord scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.
made.babel/d093468bbf8c.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|That is why it is called Babel, for there the Lord confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the Lord scattered them over the face of all the earth.
made.babel/7d5b23adc10f.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Next, God will call one man, Abram, and promise to make his name great. People could not make a great name for themselves; God gives it.
made.babel/2abec74e7a76.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The half-built tower stands alone on the empty plain. Your device hums. Time to go.
made.babel/8cc9f178fc96.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.
made.babel/262546d22c55.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Scratched into the post: the name of this land.
made.babel/1bcda14c4d12.m4a: bm_lewis|0.88|0.9|My grandfather’s grandfather knew Noah’s sons. Every family here comes from them.
made.babel/0f90f656ed7f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|All these are the clans of Noah’s sons, according to their generations and nations. From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood.
made.babel/ff5be741e29c.m4a: am_eric|1.0|0.95|Higher than the clouds! Everyone will know our name!
made.babel/9248f9c122fc.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
made.babel/873b40b0a8d6.m4a: am_liam|1.0|1.0|Hear, hear! The tower will reach the heavens!
made.babel/52174132c322.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The Lord frustrates the plans of the nations; He thwarts the devices of the peoples.
made.babel/072207ce1e50.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|A great name comes from God, not from building ourselves up. God’s plans stand, even when people’s plans fall.
made.babel/de501814c0c5.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Everyone spoke one language, and they settled on the plain of Shinar. (11:1-2)
made.babel/6e677ed3e322.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|They made bricks to build a city and a tower, to make a name for themselves. (11:3-4)
made.babel/b9420dd27a58.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The Lord came down and confused their language. (11:5-7)
made.babel/1952722142be.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|He scattered them over the earth, and the city was called Babel. (11:8-9)
made.babel/ed66d60219cc.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You, and that you made bricks for the tower.
made.babel/2c3af8fe15c1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The foreman, the builders, the crier and the old man, and the nonsense words.
made.babel/3f9a9a9af62e.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|How the tower looked. The Bible says it was meant to reach the heavens, not what shape it was.
made.babel/fc31e97c5f6e.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Genesis 11:10-32 lists the families from Noah’s son Shem down to Abram. That is where the next arc begins.
made.basket/2901d606d796.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|This story begins with a cruel law: Pharaoh orders that Hebrew baby boys be thrown into the Nile. The Bible says this in one sentence, and the game says it once. No child is hurt, and the story is about a baby who is saved.
made.basket/473e594c2867.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The device hums. Flat green fields by a wide river, and a village of mud-brick houses. The air smells of clay and smoke. Everywhere you look, people are working.
made.basket/32e4b498316b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|This is Goshen, in Egypt, hundreds of years after Joseph. The Israelites are still here.
made.basket/a04331ed5fdc.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now Joseph and all his brothers and all that generation died, but the Israelites were fruitful and increased rapidly; they multiplied and became exceedingly numerous, so that the land was filled with them.
made.basket/de979067c61d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then a new king, who did not know Joseph, came to power in Egypt.
made.basket/a8f26c734150.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|They worked the Israelites ruthlessly and made their lives bitter with hard labor in brick and mortar, and with all kinds of work in the fields. Every service they imposed was harsh.
made.basket/6c5d70f6ab03.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every son born to the Hebrews you must throw into the Nile, but every daughter you may allow to live.”
made.basket/3e16b2af0277.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|Please keep your voice down. I have been afraid for three months. Come inside, quietly, and look.
made.basket/3cfba9ae3b2f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now a man of the house of Levi married a Levite woman, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.
made.basket/30ea0010870f.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|He is getting too loud to hide. I have made up my mind. I will set him on the river, in a basket, and trust God to look after him.
made.basket/6ac1c00a86ed.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|Will you help me? I need papyrus reeds from the river bank to weave a basket, strong enough to float.
made.basket/1950d222c0f8.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|Shh. Not so loud. The baby is sleeping.
made.basket/a8fef93dde78.m4a: af_bella|1.0|1.02|I am going to watch over my little brother. Mother says I can.
made.basket/ff85d2156502.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Jochebed has not asked for the reeds yet.
made.basket/d62777aa7c09.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You cut a bundle of tall papyrus reeds and carry it up the bank.
made.basket/907779fb259b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus basket and coated it with tar and pitch.
made.basket/999d7635ee5d.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|Thank you. I have woven it as tightly as I can. Now it is time. Walk with me to the river.
made.basket/db9df3f6404b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then she placed the child in the basket and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
made.basket/c31b8f14db15.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|God, please look after my son.
made.basket/08388846ea84.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Pharaoh’s order was to throw the boys into the Nile. Jochebed put her son in the Nile, in a basket she had made herself, and left him in God’s hands.
made.basket/f196ae33e1c2.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And his sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
made.basket/0f29179eaa88.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|Miriam, stay out of sight and watch him. I cannot bear to see. Stay with her.
made.basket/4739b5441ebc.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You and Miriam wait in the reeds. The sun climbs higher. A bird calls. The basket bobs in the water. Then you hear voices.
made.basket/01f484117293.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Soon the daughter of Pharaoh went down to bathe in the Nile, and her attendants were walking along the riverbank. And when she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maidservant to retrieve it.
made.basket/22fa615e8e01.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the little boy was crying. So she had compassion on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrew children.”
made.basket/ca22feab5d80.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|The princess knew whose child this was, and what her father had ordered. She felt sorry for the baby anyway, and she did not give him up.
made.basket/3503cfbf6c64.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call one of the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”
made.basket/2e32e22c6de0.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|“Go ahead,” Pharaoh’s daughter told her. And the girl went and called the boy’s mother.
made.basket/0faedef06e2e.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages.” So the woman took the boy and nursed him.
made.basket/ab74df558f66.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Jochebed gave her baby up to the river, and then received him back, safe, and was paid to raise him. No one but God could have planned that.
made.basket/0d166bf401bf.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”
made.basket/c5e5b733ce93.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|Moses. He will grow up in Pharaoh’s palace, you, but he will always be one of us. I know it.
made.basket/ec203d3981ec.m4a: af_kore|0.95|0.96|We do not know what God will do with him. But I think the baby in the basket is more important than any of us.
made.basket/14787192ac88.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Your device hums. Time to go.
made.basket/58c3db4d3903.m4a: am_michael|0.95|0.88|We kept him hidden for three months. We were afraid, but we trusted God.
made.basket/ebb1402a4fbb.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after his birth, because they saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were unafraid of the king’s edict.
made.basket/ce0c3a473208.m4a: af_sarah|0.95|0.98|I am one of the midwives. Pharaoh told Puah and me to kill the baby boys. We could not do it. We feared God more than Pharaoh.
made.basket/656af7fc0365.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The midwives, however, feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed; they let the boys live.
made.basket/46aeadf70832.m4a: am_echo|1.0|1.0|Move! The king wants more bricks. Every Hebrew family makes a quota. I did not make the rules.
made.basket/fd20d46722b1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So the Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. As a result, they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.
made.basket/4b5a88e3e31e.m4a: am_onyx|1.0|1.05|We make bricks all day, from clay and straw. My hands are cracked from it. But the more they work us, the more of us there are.
made.basket/050e02edb60b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and flourished; so the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
made.basket/50a2b8f8cbb9.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.”
made.basket/5f77a236f552.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Jochebed did what she could, and left the rest to God. When there is nothing more you can do, you can trust the One who sees.
made.basket/581566006563.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A new king made the Israelites slaves. He ordered the Hebrew midwives, and then all his people, to kill the baby boys, but the midwives feared God. (1:8-22)
made.basket/82a6db9d7263.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|A Levite woman hid her baby for three months, then set him in a basket in the reeds, with his sister watching. (2:1-4)
made.basket/46d3c76d78dd.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Pharaoh’s daughter found him, felt sorry for him, and paid his own mother to nurse him. She named him Moses. (2:5-10)
made.basket/b0b0f24a7bb0.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You, and that you gathered the reeds and waited with Miriam.
made.basket/a65975f9e1fb.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The names Jochebed and Amram. The Bible names them in Exodus 6:20; in Exodus 2 they are only a man and woman of the house of Levi.
made.basket/59b6efb7d907.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Miriam’s age and her words. The Bible says only that Moses’ sister stood at a distance, and that she spoke to the princess.
made.basket/475ecf6c24ae.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Exodus 2:11-25: Moses, grown up, killed an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew and fled to Midian. That part comes before the burning bush.

made.covenant/f511eccef582.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Jonathan shot the arrow beyond the boy, and the two friends parted in peace. (20:35-42)
made.covenant/74f55a5a5c44.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You, and that you fetched the bow and found the arrows. In the Bible one small boy fetched them.
made.covenant/e79cdc41ae0a.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|What the people of Gibeah said about David.
made.covenant/f2b0d35b07aa.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The tambourine left by the gate.
made.covenant/dfb925619c74.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|More than once Saul threw his spear at David, and once at his own son Jonathan (18:10-11; 19:9-10; 20:33). We did not show it. Read it together with a parent.
made.cup/9c241e548dd9.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The device hums. Jacob’s camp in Canaan, the same camp you visited before, but everything is dry and brown. No rain has come, and the grain jars are empty.
made.cup/c5264468e028.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Years have gone by. Joseph’s brothers are older now, and hungrier.
made.cup/410e4486da2d.m4a: am_michael|1.0|1.02|We are running out of grain. I must do something.
made.cup/2c8f69a8c868.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you staring at one another?”
made.cup/d7225e85f386.m4a: am_michael|1.0|1.02|Look. I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.
made.cup/6e64a5b3d43b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
made.cup/5e0328e9e81c.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers, for he said, “I am afraid that harm might befall him.”
made.cup/f63a3d0811cc.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Jacob had lost Joseph. He could not bear to risk Benjamin, the only other son of his beloved Rachel.
made.cup/03a60d69338a.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Egypt. A high courtyard of cool stone, columns and servants. The brothers have walked for days to stand here. In the middle, Joseph, ruler of the land.
made.cup/e46bc004d5b2.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now Joseph was the ruler of the land; he was the one who sold grain to all its people. So when his brothers arrived, they bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.
made.cup/11d2c552cc86.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And when Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he treated them as strangers and spoke harshly to them.
made.cup/83d3674c879d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.
made.cup/394fb4c91938.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Joseph’s first dream had come true: his brothers were bowing to him. But Joseph did not seem glad. He remembered the pit.
made.cup/0fcec54b2d7e.m4a: am_puck|1.05|1.3|Joseph remembered his dreams about them and said, “You are spies! You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.”
made.cup/ba1cf7581329.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|0.95|Not so, my lord. Your servants have come to buy food. We are all sons of one man. Your servants are honest men, not spies.
made.cup/7c5c898f6d7a.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|0.95|Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.
made.cup/1a5d9a8a6c53.m4a: am_puck|1.05|1.3|And this is how you will be tested: As surely as Pharaoh lives, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
made.cup/ab8ad7a63724.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So Joseph imprisoned them for three days, and on the third day he said to them.
made.cup/cbca25a88f5b.m4a: am_puck|1.05|1.3|I fear God. So do this and you will live: If you are honest, leave one of your brothers in custody while the rest of you go and take back grain to relieve the hunger of your households. Then bring your youngest brother to me so that your words can be verified, that you may not die.
made.cup/62ef1b6d772f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then they said to one another, “Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us.”
made.cup/cff3a25d26da.m4a: am_michael|0.95|0.9|Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen. Now we must account for his blood!
made.cup/40dbfc585adc.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|They did not realize that Joseph understood them, since there was an interpreter between them.
made.cup/fd1bf331dd0a.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And he turned away from them and wept. When he turned back and spoke to them, he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.
made.cup/fbbd70ccc920.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|For twenty years the brothers had kept their secret. Now they were saying out loud what they had done. And the man they had wronged was listening, and weeping.
made.cup/0c65bde5edbb.m4a: am_puck|1.05|1.3|Please, go about your work. I have much to do.
made.cup/d079a6f205ab.m4a: am_michael|0.9|0.85|My master has asked me to look after these men.
made.cup/c3dc4301b1d8.m4a: am_puck|1.08|1.35|I have never seen a house so grand. And everyone here is so kind.
made.cup/96e43e9df6e7.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The brothers’ donkeys are not ready yet.
made.cup/0d7228de4d20.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Your hands are full. Load the donkey first.
made.cup/adbf693622be.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You lift {item}. Take it to the donkey.
made.cup/e96161c1b866.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Lift a sack of grain first.
made.cup/9ca27a91eb24.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You tie the sack tight on the donkey’s back.
made.cup/7d5a00a6a6b8.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to return each man’s silver to his sack, and to give them provisions for their journey. This order was carried out, and they loaded the grain on their donkeys and departed.
made.cup/546c5e1778c9.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|At the place where they lodged for the night, one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of the sack.
made.cup/fefb0c93656c.m4a: am_eric|1.0|1.0|My silver has been returned! It is here in my sack.
made.cup/24826b8b3a0f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Their hearts sank, and trembling, they turned to one another and said, “What is this that God has done to us?”
made.cup/b8818ef1c829.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now the famine was still severe in the land. So when Jacob’s sons had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”
made.cup/eeea2cbfb4d9.m4a: am_michael|1.0|1.02|You have deprived me of my sons. Joseph is gone and Simeon is no more. Now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is going against me!
made.cup/1e078983fea2.m4a: am_liam|0.95|0.95|The man solemnly warned us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’ If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
made.cup/a63c93b75a41.m4a: am_liam|0.95|0.95|Send the boy with me, and we will go at once, so that we may live and not die—neither we, nor you, nor our children. I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible. If I do not bring him back and set him before you, then may I bear the guilt before you all my life.
made.cup/9b1caeb0e42f.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Judah was the one who suggested selling Joseph. Now he was offering his own life for Benjamin. He had changed.
made.cup/40fd3b5d1353.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your packs and carry them down as a gift for the man—a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.
made.cup/0173db228e6a.m4a: am_michael|1.0|1.02|May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release your other brother along with Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.
made.cup/43237e5d871c.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So the men took these gifts, along with double the amount of silver, and Benjamin as well. Then they hurried down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
made.cup/6a1443d60ccc.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When Joseph saw Benjamin with his brothers, he said to the steward of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they shall dine with me at noon.”
made.cup/b3f4d1d14977.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The steward asks you to help serve the meal. Benjamin is to be given plenty.
made.cup/aeddc3b35b14.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The meal has not been served yet.
made.cup/aaf36b8693c1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Your hands are full. Take that plate to Benjamin first.
made.cup/a6c914271a2b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|There is nothing there to lift.
made.cup/01fe27e71e6a.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You lift {item}. Take it to Benjamin.
made.cup/51263f771de1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Pick up a plate of food first.
made.cup/20703baeb190.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Benjamin’s eyes get wider with every plate.
made.cup/b5d1037b12e6.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|They were seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn to the youngest, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.
made.cup/fecb7e1bd045.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When the portions were served to them from Joseph’s table, Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of the others. So they feasted and drank freely with Joseph.
made.cup/d3087ddb8e2b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother’s son, he asked, “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” Then he declared, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”
made.cup/218b4bb02db2.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Joseph hurried out because he was moved to tears for his brother, and he went to a private room to weep.
made.cup/a2dee4126794.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then Joseph instructed his steward: “Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each one’s silver in the mouth of his sack. Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack, along with the silver for his grain.” So the steward did as Joseph had instructed.
made.cup/8f8fdb739275.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Joseph is putting his brothers to one more test. He wants to know whether they will abandon Benjamin, as they once abandoned him.
made.cup/f0762a826755.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|At daybreak, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys. They had not gone far from the city when Joseph told his steward, “Pursue the men at once, and when you overtake them, ask, ‘Why have you repaid good with evil?
made.cup/444a8bdeebcd.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|0.95|We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found in the mouths of our sacks. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?
made.cup/420d22b42dde.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The steward searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest—and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
made.cup/8b217586aa52.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then they all tore their clothes, loaded their donkeys, and returned to the city.
made.cup/9795cf627ed7.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When Judah and his brothers arrived at Joseph’s house, he was still there, and they fell to the ground before him.
made.cup/0b1570811227.m4a: am_puck|1.05|1.3|What is this deed you have done?
made.cup/ce6063c6d4bc.m4a: am_liam|0.95|0.95|What can we say to my lord? How can we plead? How can we justify ourselves? God has exposed the iniquity of your servants. We are now my lord’s slaves—both we and the one who was found with the cup.
made.cup/29c697563163.m4a: am_puck|1.05|1.3|Far be it from me to do this. The man who was found with the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may return to your father in peace.
made.cup/c10773747f90.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then Judah approached Joseph and said, “Sir, please let your servant speak personally to my lord.
made.cup/82e24c507158.m4a: am_liam|0.95|0.95|your servant guaranteed the boy’s safety to my father, saying, ‘If I do not return him to you, I will bear the guilt before you, my father, all my life.’
made.cup/18caee1855c0.m4a: am_liam|0.95|0.95|Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy. Let him return with his brothers. For how can I go back to my father without the boy? I could not bear to see the misery that would overwhelm him.
made.cup/64db9bec491f.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|Twenty years earlier, Judah had helped sell a brother and let his father believe he was dead. Now he offered to become a slave so his father would not lose another son.
made.cup/41256395f8ca.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The courtyard is silent. Joseph’s face is working. He cannot speak.
made.cup/99fb56f299d2.m4a: am_liam|0.95|0.95|I have never been so afraid in all my life. And I think the man in charge is about to say something important.
made.cup/1e7965579e04.m4a: bm_fable|1.0|1.0|The brothers speak Hebrew, my master speaks Egyptian, and I stand in between. But he understands every word they say. I think he has been listening more closely than any of them know.
made.cup/9be437cd865e.m4a: am_liam|1.0|1.0|Egyptians do not eat with Hebrews, so we serve them at separate tables. But the master has put the brothers in order by age, exactly right. It is as if he knows them.
made.cup/23e8f7c129d4.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|They ate separately because the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them.
made.cup/c0e0eb160bc9.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy. Let him return with his brothers.
made.cup/20be59d8836f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy.
made.cup/ab5bea6efecb.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|The brothers who once sold Joseph were not the same men who now stood in the courtyard. Judah would give up his own freedom for Benjamin. Real change shows when we are tested again.
made.cup/4fc93e08e5d9.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Jacob sent ten sons to Egypt for grain and kept Benjamin at home. The brothers bowed to Joseph, who did not tell them who he was. (42:1-9)
made.cup/ab131e4442aa.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Joseph accused them of being spies, put them in prison for three days and kept Simeon until they returned with Benjamin. They talked about what they had done to Joseph. (42:10-24)
made.cup/3475e973a247.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|On their second trip, Judah promised to be responsible for Benjamin. Joseph gave them a feast. (43:1-34)
made.cup/281480bef74d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Joseph’s silver cup was put in Benjamin’s sack. When it was found, Judah offered himself as a slave instead. (44:1-34)
made.cup/3adc39db110f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You, and that you loaded the donkeys and served Benjamin’s plates. The Bible says only that Benjamin’s portion was five times larger.
made.cup/a2d5c0d597be.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The interpreter, the servant and the brothers’ names: only Reuben, Simeon, Judah and Benjamin are named in this part of the Bible.
made.cup/31e1e40b33ad.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|How long the journeys took. Canaan to Egypt is a few weeks on foot.
made.cup/bde6b3a6b2eb.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Genesis 42:36-38: Jacob first refused to let Benjamin go, and Reuben offered his own sons as a pledge. The game tells only Judah’s pledge in Genesis 43.
made.dagon/3a7845ed26cb.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|This story includes a battle in which many Israelites die, the deaths of Eli’s sons, a plague in the Philistine cities, and, later, a judgment in which seventy men died for looking inside the ark. The game names these things in short, plain sentences from the Bible. It does not show them.
made.dagon/1326a992fc1b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The device hums. A dusty plain, a long way from Shiloh, with a rough camp of tents and a mood of fear. Soldiers sit on the ground with their heads in their hands. Not far away, over a low hill, the Philistines have set up their own camp, and there are far more of them.
made.dagon/9914cdbe4ceb.m4a: bm_george|0.9|0.85|We have lost four thousand men. We have to do something.
made.dagon/6047ad4a1cd7.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Thus the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now the Israelites went out to meet the Philistines in battle and camped at Ebenezer, while the Philistines camped at Aphek.
made.dagon/245fc1235ee3.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The Philistines arrayed themselves against Israel, and as the battle spread, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the battlefield.
made.dagon/334a916d4eb1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When the troops returned to the camp, the elders of Israel asked, “Why has the Lord brought defeat on us before the Philistines today? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Shiloh, so that it may go with us to save us from the hand of our enemies.”
made.dagon/72b9ca71fc71.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|The elders asked why the Lord had let them lose. But they did not ask the Lord. They decided that the ark would work like a good-luck charm. God is not a charm.
made.dagon/2e930d98072e.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So the people sent men to Shiloh, and they brought back the ark of the covenant of the Lord of Hosts, who sits enthroned between the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
made.dagon/c0ce86151c6f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When the ark of the covenant of the Lord entered the camp, all the Israelites raised such a great shout that the ground shook.
made.dagon/c830044817e0.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|On hearing the noise of the shout, the Philistines asked, “What is this loud shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?” And when they realized that the ark of the Lord had entered the camp, the Philistines were afraid.
made.dagon/66ff1ffe9348.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|0.88|The gods have entered their camp! Woe to us, for nothing like this has happened before. Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
made.dagon/c9abcc67ae4c.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|0.88|Take courage and be men, O Philistines! Otherwise, you will serve the Hebrews just as they served you. Now be men and fight!
made.dagon/67fcd10633ef.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great—thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell. The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
made.dagon/548eea71c65f.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And she named the boy Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” because the ark of God had been captured and her father-in-law and her husband had been killed.
made.dagon/045ff05bf911.m4a: af_kore|1.0|1.0|The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured.
made.dagon/88d10563d92b.m4a: bf_emma|0.95|1.0|The ark was just a box. God was not trapped in it, and He was not inside the Philistines’ hands. But the people had begun to treat it as if it were the same as God. The next part of the story shows who was in charge.
made.dagon/4077f26659d9.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|After the Philistines had captured the ark of God, they took it from Ebenezer to Ashdod, carried it into the temple of Dagon, and set it beside his statue.
made.dagon/97e6bfbb479b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The Philistine temple at Ashdod is huge and dim, with columns and heavy shadows. At the far end stands a great statue of Dagon, their god, half man and half fish. Beside it, rather small by comparison, stands the golden ark.
made.dagon/5caf340884d1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the Lord.
made.dagon/e094e1f18a7a.m4a: am_echo|1.0|1.0|We stood him up again. Do not tell anyone he fell.
made.dagon/34f4ea0f6a1e.m4a: am_onyx|1.0|1.05|We must decide what to do.
made.dagon/8404dda1accf.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The statue of Dagon, fallen on its face.
made.dagon/270f0ef4e6ce.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|You and the priests heave the heavy statue back onto its stand.
made.dagon/6631e17d895d.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So they took Dagon and returned him to his place.
made.dagon/b2d2aced79bc.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|But when they got up early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen on his face before the ark of the Lord, with his head and his hands broken off and lying on the threshold. Only the torso remained.
made.dagon/7c358ac238dd.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|That is why, to this day, the priests of Dagon and all who enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod do not step on the threshold.
made.dagon/8a85d0fb585b.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now the hand of the Lord was heavy on the people of Ashdod and its vicinity, ravaging them and afflicting them with tumors.
made.dagon/05522891b451.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|And when the men of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel must not stay here with us, because His hand is heavy upon us and upon our god Dagon.” So they called together all the rulers of the Philistines and asked, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” “It must be moved to Gath,” they replied.
made.dagon/bd79556ec459.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|So they sent the ark of God to Ekron, but as it arrived, the Ekronites cried out, “They have brought us the ark of the God of Israel in order to kill us and our people!”
made.dagon/ec2fed816ef1.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Then the Ekronites called together all the rulers of the Philistines and said, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel. It must return to its place, so that it will not kill us and our people!”
made.dagon/b2588a608c0e.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|When the ark of the Lord had been in the land of the Philistines seven months, the Philistines summoned the priests and diviners, saying, “What shall we do with the ark of the Lord? Tell us how to send it back to its place.”
made.dagon/d9f0ba1b7c04.m4a: am_michael|1.0|1.0|If you return the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but by all means return it to Him with a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and you will understand why His hand has not been lifted from you.
made.dagon/c5112a7cd6c8.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|Now, therefore, prepare one new cart with two milk cows that have never been yoked. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves away and pen them up.
made.dagon/fe2dceaf77b0.m4a: am_fenrir|1.0|1.05|We need to test this. Cows will not leave their calves, so the calves must be taken away. Would you help?
made.dagon/1279b5325961.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|There are no calves to pen yet.

made.dagon/bcecb33957f3.m4a: af_heart|0.95|1.0|The two cows stand in the yoke, restless. They have never pulled a cart. Every instinct will make them turn back toward their calves.
